titleEn: The Gāyatrī asks the Sun for one thing — light up our thinking. That is the whole prayer.
sanskrit: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः । तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥
transliteration: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ · tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi · dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt
meaningEn: Oṃ. Earth, sky, heaven. On that finest light of Savitṛ — the Sun who sets everything moving — we meditate. May he set our thoughts moving too. It asks for one thing only: a lit-up mind.
meaningHi: ॐ। धरती, आकाश, स्वर्ग। उस सूरज देवता की — जो सबको चलाता है — सबसे बढ़िया रोशनी पर हम ध्यान लगाते हैं। वह हमारी सोच को भी आगे बढ़ाए। बस एक चीज़ माँगी है — रोशन दिमाग़।
sayItLike: Om bhoor bhu-vah svah · tat sa-vi-tur va-ren-yam · bhar-go de-vas-ya dhee-ma-hi · dhi-yo yo nah pra-cho-da-yaat

words.grammar: bhūḥ — the -ḥ turns to -r before the next vowel (sandhi); first of the three 'worlds' (vyāhṛti)
third vyāhṛti; the three together are the Yajurvedic prefix, not part of the Ṛgveda verse

words.glossEn: of Savitṛ — the Sun as the one who sets all things going
words.glossHi: सविता का — सूरज, जो सबको चलाता है
words.root: √sū — to impel, set in motion; Savitṛ is 'the Impeller'
words.grammar: of Savitṛ — genitive; savituḥ becomes savitur before a vowel
describes 'bhargo' (that light) — both are neuter, both point at the light
bhargaḥ becomes bhargo before a voiced sound; the thing we meditate on

words.glossEn: of the god — the shining one
words.grammar: of the deva — genitive, hence -asya; goes with savitur

words.root: √dhī / dhyai — to think, meditate (or √dhā, to hold)
words.grammar: we-may-meditate — first person plural, a wish; the only verb in the first line
dhiyaḥ becomes dhiyo before a voiced sound; the object of 'pracodayāt'
yaḥ becomes yo before a voiced sound; refers back to Savitṛ

words.glossEn: may he set in motion — may he inspire
words.root: pra + √cud — to push forward, urge on
words.grammar: may-he-impel — third person, a wish; the ask of the whole mantra

source.ref: 3.62.10 (seer: Viśvāmitra); the oṃ + bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ prefix is Yajurvedic sandhyā liturgy (cf. Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 2.11)
source.note: In the Ṛgveda the verse is addressed to Savitṛ, the impelling Sun; the goddess Gāyatrī as a person is later Purāṇic devotion. Taught here without Vedic accents (svara); traditional recitation adds them.

significance.textSays: Ṛgveda 3.62.10: 'On that finest light of the god Savitṛ may we meditate; may he set our thoughts in motion.' A wish for a lit-up mind — nothing else is asked.
significance.traditionSays: Recited at the three sandhyās — dawn, noon, dusk — and given at the sacred-thread ceremony; called the mother of the Vedas. Historic rules limited who could recite it; the stance here is that everyone may learn it, free.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That reciting it brings any result. It is a prayer for clear thought, quoted exactly and taught word by word.

practice.timeOfDay: sandhyā — dawn, noon, dusk; dawn if only one
